recent_commits.message: Add Python support to reproducibility_check
recent_commits.body:
Extends the module to assess and (optionally) execute Python code
alongside R, mirroring the existing R pipeline's static analysis,
execution, and reporting:

- code_file_refs()/code_library_names() (R/code_check.R): Python write-
  call detection (to_csv/savefig/np.save/pickle.dump/...), alongside the
  existing Python read/import support.
- repro_file_io()/repro_rewrite_paths()/repro_write_scripts()
  (R/reproducibility_check.R): now accept lang = "Python" -- read/write/
  path-rewrite detection, os.chdir() stripping (Python's setwd()
  equivalent), and a full Python port of the write-redirect logic
  (os.path.join()-aware). Font-substitution and library() injection
  stay R-only (no Python equivalent exists for either).
- New R/reproducibility_check_python.R: repro_dependencies_py()
  (import + requirements.txt/pyproject.toml parsing), a static Python
  stdlib module list, repro_install_deps_py()/repro_run_scripts_py()
  (pip/process-based execution backend, mirroring the R callr backend
  but running each script whole -- no per-statement object capture).
- New R/reproducibility_check_python_docker.R: the Docker-sandboxed
  mirror, reusing the existing generic container-lifecycle helpers
  (non-root uid, container-name/stop-on-timeout, resource limits).
- A Python corrective re-run step (reorders scripts to resolve a
  NameError to another script's top-level definition) -- confirmed via
  testing that, unlike R's shared-session corrective reorder, this can
  never actually fix a genuine Python NameError (each script runs as
  its own OS process with no shared namespace); documented as a known,
  structural limitation rather than removed.
- Python scripts' stdout now feeds the same STATO-typed "Reported vs.
  reproduced" matching R output does, via the already-existing
  .ipynb_stat_line()/.ipynb_stat_table() text parsers (built for
  Jupyter notebook cells, reused here against live execution output) --
  no new statistics-extraction code needed.
- inst/modules/reproducibility_check.R: replaces the hard R-only
  language gate with a dispatch that runs the R and Python pipelines
  in parallel and merges their table/summary_table/report/traffic_light
  into one result.

New Python test fixtures (tests/testthat/fixtures/repro/*.py) and unit/
module-level tests mirroring the existing R ones; Docker/interpreter-
gated tests skip cleanly when unavailable. 247 tests passing.

it: the 12.x reader keeps the extraction block whole. This adds a 12.1
export the Platform returned, of a CC BY 4.0 paper, and tests that a
citation resolves to its reference by target_id, that captions and notes

12.x file in one folder, still read in the older format.

extract the paper again with a bibr version that writes 12.x, or, for a
newer schema, update metacheck.

recent_commits.body:
Registry additions, each live-checked 2026-10-05:
- Figshare: data.lib.vt.edu (VTechData), agdatacommons.nal.usda.gov (USDA Ag
  Data Commons), adelaide.figshare.com (U. Adelaide), plus the missing DOI

- DSpace legacy: datastorre.stir.ac.uk (U. Stirling).
- DSpace 7+: ecommons.cornell.edu, and www.repository.cam.ac.uk (Apollo,
  U. Cambridge) via a new UI-host -> API-host alias mechanism
  (.dspace7_api_host_aliases()), since Cambridge's citable host doesn't
  itself serve /server/api.

Three entries from the issue were NOT added after failing live
verification from here, and are documented in code comments instead of
silently added or silently dropped:
- science-data.hu (Dataverse): could not determine whether its identifier
  is DOI-shaped or a true non-DOI handle prefix; the host itself did not
  respond to any endpoint tried.
- researchdata.se (Dataverse, SND): a real DataCite client, but every
  /api/info/version path tried 404s or fails to resolve; could not
  reproduce the issue's live confirmation.
- EDI (DataONE, portal.edirepository.org / pasta.lternet.edu, 10.6073):
  confirmed live to run PASTA, not Metacat -- does not expose the
  "<api_base>object/<pid>" shape every other DataONE host here relies on.
  Needs real URL-construction logic for PASTA's own API shape, not a
  table entry.
- ecommons.cornell.edu was proposed under DSpace legacy by the issue, but
  confirmed live to be DSpace 7+ (DSpace-CRIS) instead; added there, not
  to the legacy list.

Also adds tests/testthat/test-archive-{4tu,dspace7,fsd,gitlab,mendeley,
reshare}.R, the six archive-*.R modules with no prior test coverage at
all. Mostly offline unit tests (link detection, id/host/handle
extraction) plus one live smoke test per file against a real, stable
public item, matching the existing figshare/dataone test convention.
Surfaced two pre-existing issues along the way, documented in test
comments rather than fixed: .fsd_study_id() is not vectorised (errors on
length>1 input, unlike every sibling id-extractor), and .mendeley_info()
does not classify a well-formed-but-nonexistent dataset id as an error
(Mendeley's API returns HTTP 200 with the real 404 only inside the JSON
body).

recent_commits.message: Remove the date-format file-naming rule; relabel severity for display
recent_commits.body:
The date-format rule flagged any 8-digit run in a filename that failed to
parse as YYYYMMDD. There is no reliable way to tell, from the filename
alone, whether an 8-digit run was ever intended as a date rather than some
other numeric ID (a DOI suffix, an accession number, a participant code),
so the heuristic produced false positives with no way to avoid them (#462,
a 16-digit ID sliced into two bogus "invalid date" violations). Removed
rather than patched further.

Also relabels the naming-issues table's Severity column from the internal
"bad"/"suggestion" values to "Required"/"Suggestion" for display, without
changing the underlying severity classification or any gating logic.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Redesign the brief/simple report: statement-style layout, fold findings by file, trim redundant summary lines
recent_commits.body:
The brief to-do list previously split a check's problem from its location
across separate tables/groups (e.g. "N items: Status: absent" followed by
quoted "sentences" that were actually bare file names), duplicated counts
already stated in the module summary, and always printed a confirmation
line for checks that found nothing. code_check's and repo_check's
per-finding bullets are now folded by file, naming both what was found and
where in one line, with the flagged values bolded; parse-error and other
free-text findings are collapsed to a single line instead of breaking
across the rendered table's embedded line breaks. code_check.R and
codebook_check.R drop the always-on "nothing found" / redundant headline
lines from their brief summary_text, and code_check.R's version-pin
summary adds a one-line remediation suggestion.

The simple (email-safe, static) report gets a bank-statement-style visual
redesign: a full-bleed brand-green banner with the Metacheck logo (embedded
as a base64 data URI so the report stays a single self-contained file) and
a dot-pattern texture, ledger-style summary rows with a left accent stripe
per traffic light, and restyled tables/callouts to match. Fixes several
bugs surfaced along the way: a Pandoc header-attribute id built from a
module title containing parentheses broke and leaked literal `{#id}`
syntax into the rendered heading/TOC; the brief-mode header rewrite
stripped the banner entirely since it used to cut everything after
`</style>`; and the template's own CSS pushed `sprintf()`'s format-string
past its 8192-character limit, crashing the render, so the header
templating was switched to length-safe sequential substitution.

recent_commits.message: Extend GROBID DOI-whitespace fix to more safe anchors (#458)
recent_commits.body:
#411's fix only collapsed two corruption shapes (https ://..., doi.
org/...). A 50-paper re-validation found 23 papers still corrupted by
the same line-wrap artifact at a different position. This adds more
anchors with the same safety property (a fixed literal substring that
never occurs in ordinary prose): a DOI's "10.NNNN/" prefix, benefiting
every platform's bare-DOI detector, plus the single-fixed-host
literals zenodo.org/, osf.io/, and researchbox.org/ and the /dryad./
and /zenodo. suffix shapes. Resolves 10 of the 23 papers; the rest
need either line-wrap position info GROBID doesn't currently expose,
or live API disambiguation -- not a text-normalization fix.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Add a brief report_type() for a fast, actionable to-do list
recent_commits.body:
report_type() gains "brief" and "simple_brief" values alongside the
existing "full"/"simple" -- an orthogonal axis (content amount vs.
rendering mechanics) that trims a report down to only flagged
modules, grouped by the specific issue found, with the actual
offending text/file quoted. Several modules (power.R, code_check.R,
data_check.R) needed their own bullet renderers rather than one
fully generic heuristic, since what counts as "an issue" vs. normal
output varies per module in ways no shared column convention
captures.

Also redesigns the plain/email-safe template's CSS (the old
"margin-left: -20px" rule had nothing to push against on a
Bootstrap-free page, running headings off-screen), adds a
"How It Works" link to each module's online manual chapter, and adds
data-raw/report-all-types.R to render all four report types from one
module run for comparison.

commit addresses the remaining, still-live gaps confirmed against current
dev:

  to TRUE; an AND can only narrow an already-TRUE value, so every unopened

recent_commits.message: Warn and self-explain when a Dryad API key is missing
recent_commits.body:
Dryad allows listing a dataset's files without a key, but requires one
(dryad_pat()/dryad_auth()) to download file bytes even from a fully
public dataset. data_check and code_check depend on those bytes, so a
missing key silently zeroed out columns/code analysis with only a bare
"HTTP 401" to go on.

Now a one-time session message fires as soon as a Dryad dataset is
resolved with no key set, and a 401 caused by a missing key is named
explicitly in the download-failure report instead of a bare HTTP
status. Documented the limitation in repo_check/data_check/code_check.

Also fixes two unrelated issues found while verifying this change:
- osf_file_download() crashed with "could not find function
  cap_report" (missing leading dot) whenever a repo's per-repository
  download budget was hit with files still remaining.
- A live OSF fixture test had stale expected paths after the real
  project's folder structure changed; and a stale/missing CrossRef
  mock fixture made the "longer bib" test fail.

recent_commits.message: Label an unmatched subscripted Hedges' g_av as indeterminate, not no_match
recent_commits.body:
d_z and d_rm(r=0.5) are fully determined by t and df alone, so a
reported value that doesn't match either really is a confirmed
inconsistency. Hedges' g_av (Cumming, 2012's bias-corrected
average-variance standardizer) also depends on the individual
condition SDs and the true observed correlation between them --
information a bare t(df) does not preserve -- so a correctly-computed
g_av can legitimately fail every tested formula without being wrong.
Reusing "no_match" for both cases made a verified-correct g_av
indistinguishable from a real reporting error.

When the reported effect size is an explicitly subscripted Hedges' g
(g_av/g_z/g_rm/gs -- not bare, unsubscripted "g", which is ambiguous
with the original Hedges, 1981 correction that IS a deterministic
multiplier of d) and matches none of the three tested formulas, label
it "indeterminate" (cannot verify) instead of "no_match" (verified and
inconsistent) -- the same distinction the module already draws for a
Welch's t-test's non-integer df.

Also normalizes parse_d_stats()'s label before checking it: without an
apostrophe ("Hedges g av" vs "Hedges' g av", as GROBID sometimes
renders it), the whole phrase is captured as one label rather than
just "g av", so a leading Hedges'/Cohen's word is stripped first (#455).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

recent_commits.message: Fix #448 follow-up: bare "g av"/"g_av" with no Hedges'/Cohen's prefix
recent_commits.body:
The previous #448 fix only extended extract_eq()'s match when the
"Hedges'"/"Cohen's" prefix word was present before the collapsed
subscript. A bare "g av" or literal-underscore "g_av"/"d_z" (no prefix
word at all -- as can happen on a second mention or in a table cell)
still fell through to the original bug, mis-parsing "av"/"z"/etc. as
an unrelated standalone statistic.

Added a second, narrowly-scoped alternative to extract_eq()'s pattern:
a bare "g"/"d" immediately followed by one of its own known subscript
words (av/z/rm/s), gated to exactly that letter+word pairing rather
than "one extra word after any statistic name" -- the latter would
also fuse unrelated adjacent words that happen to precede a number
("sample size n = 40" -> "size n", "mean age years = 25" -> "age
years"), confirmed by testing both sentences directly.

Also extended stat_effect_size's parse_d_stats() numeric-value regex
to accept a literal underscore (not just whitespace) between the
letter and its subscript suffix, so "g_av"/"d_z" written with an
underscore -- not only GROBID's space-collapsed form -- has its value
parsed for coherence checking rather than being recognized as an
effect size but reported as unparseable.

recent_commits.message: Shorten the function documentation
recent_commits.body:
* Every exported function's roxygen block is rewritten to state what the
  function does, its arguments, and its value, without history, repeated
  rationale, or figurative language. Rd files regenerated; no
  documentation warnings, all examples run.
* `?audit` and `?audit-special` now list the percentage and sum

recent_commits.message: Revise the vignettes for 1.0.0
recent_commits.body:
* `vignette("rounding-in-depth")` misattributed the downward mean of
  `round(seq(4.5, 10.5))` to floating-point error. Those ties are exact;
  the parity rule only preserves the mean if as many ties are rounded
  down as up. The section now separates exact ties at whole numbers
  from the inexact decimal case, and the vignette covers the
  `round_ties_*()` functions, the full IEEE 754 table, and `unround()`
  as the tests actually use it (`digits`, all three tests).
* The GRIM, GRIMMER, and DEBIT vignettes are rewritten in a plainer
  style around the same examples, without `pkgload::load_all()` in the
  setup chunk, and the DEBIT one documents `formula`.
* The in-depth, simple, devtools, and rounding-options vignettes are
  trimmed, and outdated statements corrected: mappers reject non-tibble
  data frames, `n` may come back integer, and `Vectorize()` is not how
  the three tests are vectorized.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Condense the 1.0.0 NEWS entry
recent_commits.body:
* The entry ran to 465 lines, with a paragraph of before-and-after
  detail for every fix. It is now 134 lines: numeric inputs and
  `digits_*` lead the breaking changes, changes to test results are
  grouped by cause, and bugfixes are grouped by subsystem with one or
  two sentences each. Internal-only changes and trivial message fixes
  are dropped.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Name unconventional rounding as a possible cause in `?is_percentage_of`
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Say what an inconsistent percentage shows, and fix an ambiguous `function_map()` doc
recent_commits.body:
* An inconsistency means the reported values can't all be correct. The
section in `?is_percentage_of` now says so, and that the test doesn't
show why, instead of suggesting that the values may be correct after all.

* `.reported_variadic` itself defaults to `NULL`. The sentence about
having no default refers to the argument of the factory-made function,
and now says so.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Shorten the section on trivial explanations of percentage mismatches
recent_commits.body:
* Plain sentences instead of a list, and no claim about how common such
explanations are, which nobody has measured.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Warn that inconsistent percentages often have innocent causes
recent_commits.body:
* A new section of `?is_percentage_of` lists the common ones: a
different denominator, a sample size that changed between analyses,
and other rounding. It points to `is_percentage_of_map_seq(var = "n")`
for finding the denominator that fits.

* `?is_percentage_of_map` links to that section.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Revive the baseline consistency tests for percentages and sums
recent_commits.body:
* `is_percentage_of()` checks whether a reported percentage is what a
reported count out of `n` would be reported as. It reuses GRIM's
`sum_range()`, so it runs in exact integer arithmetic under any rounding
method. `is_percentage_of_map()` and `is_percentage_of_map_seq()` lift it
to the mapper tiers.

* `add_up_to()` checks whether counts sum to their total, returning `NA`
for fractional values, whose sums are not exact. `add_up_to_map()` is
the first mapper built with `function_map(.reported_variadic)` (#42).

* Both get `audit()` methods. `error_digits_missing()` shows an example
call with the percentage test's own arguments.

* Replace the test file that had been commented out since 2023 with an
exact-oracle test, a check against GRIM, and mapper tests.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Compute the confidence interval that `grim_binomial(conf.level)` names
recent_commits.body:
* `conf.level` used to be echoed into a column with no interval behind
it. The output now has `conf.low` and `conf.high`: the exact
Clopper-Pearson interval around `estimate` from `stats::binom.test()`,
one-sided like the test.

* An invalid `conf.level` is now an error naming `grim_binomial()`.

recent_commits.message: Throw all user-facing errors via `abort_in_export()`
recent_commits.body:
* Converted the 33 `cli::cli_abort()` calls with `call = rlang::caller_env()`
  or a `call` parameter, which blamed whatever function called the check:
  an internal helper if one was in between, or `seq_disperse()` within
  `grim_map_seq()`. Dropped the `call` parameters of
  `abort_symmetric_invalid()`, `check_comb_value()`,
  `check_decidable_n_items()`, and `recycle_length_common()`.
* Converted 17 more input checks without a `call`, which blamed themselves,
  e.g. "Error in `check_debit_inputs()`" for `debit_map()`.
* `vectorize_test()` no longer builds the wrapper's call for errors, and its
  mapper hint names `grim_map()` under `lapply()`, not `FUN_map()`.
* Left internal errors and the generic `class_with()` and `call_on()` as
  they were.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Fix two misattributed error messages in `reround()` and the dispersers
recent_commits.body:
* An invalid `rounding` string in `reround()` named the internal
  `reconstruct_rounded_numbers_scalar()`; it now goes through
  `abort_in_export()`.
* A non-numeric `dispersion` in `seq_disperse()` and `disperse()` failed in
  base R's `round()`; both now check its type first.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Attribute errors in mapper and factory helpers to the user-called function
recent_commits.body:
* Replaced the hard-coded frame counts of `name_caller_call(n = 2L)`,
  `(n = 3L)`, and `error_digits_flawed()`'s `rlang::caller_env(4)` by
  `name_last_export_code()` and `abort_in_export()`. Errors used to say,
  e.g., "Error in `check_factory_dots()`" and named `FUN()` under
  `lapply()`; they now name `grim_map()` either way.
* Added jarl.toml so that jarl accepts repeated bullet names in
  `abort_in_export()`, as it does for cli functions.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Fix #93: name the user-called function in `digits_*` errors
recent_commits.body:
* `check_newly_numeric()` and `error_digits_missing()` use
  `name_last_export()` and `index_last_export()` instead of
  `caller_test_fn()`, which matched names against a pattern and so took
  `grim_plot()` for the culprit in `grim_plot(grim_map(x))`.
* Updated the standalone file: it now finds the innermost export not called by
  package code, so a lazily evaluated argument like `grim_map(x)` above is
  named itself. Under `lapply()`, the name is the export's own, not `FUN`.
* Removed `caller_test_fn()` and `PATTERN_NAME_TEST_FN`.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Attribute the invalid `rounding` error to the user-called function
recent_commits.body:
* `bound_numerators()` now throws it via `abort_in_export()`, so it names
  e.g. `grim_map()` rather than an internal helper.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Import standalone last-export file from unsum
recent_commits.body:
* `abort_in_export()` and `arg_match_in_export()` attribute errors to the
  exported function the user called, found on the call stack by identity.
* Requires cli (>= 3.0.0) for `cli_abort()`.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Dissolve helper to simplify code
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Test that `grimmer_plot_values()` draws every valid input
recent_commits.body:
* `plot_comb()` would fail on an `NA` from `grimmer()`. Each input that
  makes it return `NA` is rejected up front today; a grid over the edges
  catches a future `NA` branch in `grimmer_scalar()` without a matching
  check.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Stop guessing where a mapper with disabled args was made
recent_commits.body:
* Through `lapply()`, the error said that `FUN()` was created within
  some package, found by `getAnywhere()` on that name. It now names the
  function factory's `.args_disabled` argument and nothing else.
* Remove a stray sentence fragment from the docs.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

repos.readme_excerpt:
**Text, section, table and statistic extraction from academic papers (PDF, DOCX, HTML), built
for meta-science.**

docpluck turns a research article into text you can run statistical checks on. It extracts the
text layer, repairs the damage extraction itself causes (lost minus signs, split ligatures,
interleaved columns, Greek letters decoded as Latin), identifies the paper's sections, pulls
tables out as cell grids, flattens table rows into records a statistics checker can read, and
renders the whole paper as Markdown. Every output carries a record of what the library had to
guess or refused

highlights.message: Add Python support to reproducibility_check
highlights.body:
Extends the module to assess and (optionally) execute Python code
alongside R, mirroring the existing R pipeline's static analysis,
execution, and reporting:

- code_file_refs()/code_library_names() (R/code_check.R): Python write-
  call detection (to_csv/savefig/np.save/pickle.dump/...), alongside the
  existing Python read/import support.
- repro_file_io()/repro_rewrite_paths()/repro_write_scripts()
  (R/reproducibility_check.R): now accept lang = "Python" -- read/write/
  path-rewrite detection, os.chdir() stripping (Python's setwd()
  equivalent), and a full Python port of the write-redirect logic
  (os.path.join()-aware). Font-substitution and library() injection
  stay R-only (no Python equivalent exists for either).
- New R/reproducibility_check_python.R: repro_dependencies_py()
  (import + requirements.txt/pyproject.toml parsing), a static Python
  stdlib module list, repro_install_deps_py()/repro_run_scripts_py()
  (pip/process-based execution backend, mirroring the R callr backend
  but running each script whole -- no per-statement object capture).
- New R/reproducibility_check_python_docker.R: the Docker-sandboxed
  mirror, reusing the existing generic container-lifecycle helpers
  (non-root uid, container-name/stop-on-timeout, resource limits).
- A Python corrective re-run step (reorders scripts to resolve a
  NameError to another script's top-level definition) -- confirmed via
  testing that, unlike R's shared-session corrective reorder, this can
  never actually fix a genuine Python NameError (each script runs as
  its own OS process with no shared namespace); documented as a known,
  structural limitation rather than removed.
- Python scripts' stdout now feeds the same STATO-typed "Reported vs.
  reproduced" matching R output does, via the already-existing
  .ipynb_stat_line()/.ipynb_stat_table() text parsers (built for
  Jupyter notebook cells, reused here against live execution output) --
  no new statistics-extraction code needed.
- inst/modules/reproducibility_check.R: replaces the hard R-only
  language gate with a dispatch that runs the R and Python pipelines
  in parallel and merges their table/summary_table/report/traffic_light
  into one result.

New Python test fixtures (tests/testthat/fixtures/repro/*.py) and unit/
module-level tests mirroring the existing R ones; Docker/interpreter-
gated tests skip cleanly when unavailable. 247 tests passing.

highlights.message: Add confirmed registry entries from issue #461; add test coverage for 6 untested archive modules
highlights.body:
Registry additions, each live-checked 2026-10-05:
- Figshare: data.lib.vt.edu (VTechData), agdatacommons.nal.usda.gov (USDA Ag
  Data Commons), adelaide.figshare.com (U. Adelaide), plus the missing DOI
  prefix (10.5522) for the already-listed rdr.ucl.ac.uk (UCL).
- DSpace legacy: datastorre.stir.ac.uk (U. Stirling).
- DSpace 7+: ecommons.cornell.edu, and www.repository.cam.ac.uk (Apollo,
  U. Cambridge) via a new UI-host -> API-host alias mechanism
  (.dspace7_api_host_aliases()), since Cambridge's citable host doesn't
  itself serve /server/api.

Three entries from the issue were NOT added after failing live
verification from here, and are documented in code comments instead of
silently added or silently dropped:
- science-data.hu (Dataverse): could not determine whether its identifier
  is DOI-shaped or a true non-DOI handle prefix; the host itself did not
  respond to any endpoint tried.
- researchdata.se (Dataverse, SND): a real DataCite client, but every
  /api/info/version path tried 404s or fails to resolve; could not
  reproduce the issue's live confirmation.
- EDI (DataONE, portal.edirepository.org / pasta.lternet.edu, 10.6073):
  confirmed live to run PASTA, not Metacat -- does not expose the
  "<api_base>object/<pid>" shape every other DataONE host here relies on.
  Needs real URL-construction logic for PASTA's own API shape, not a
  table entry.
- ecommons.cornell.edu was proposed under DSpace legacy by the issue, but
  confirmed live to be DSpace 7+ (DSpace-CRIS) instead; added there, not
  to the legacy list.

Also adds tests/testthat/test-archive-{4tu,dspace7,fsd,gitlab,mendeley,
reshare}.R, the six archive-*.R modules with no prior test coverage at
all. Mostly offline unit tests (link detection, id/host/handle
extraction) plus one live smoke test per file against a real, stable
public item, matching the existing figshare/dataone test convention.
Surfaced two pre-existing issues along the way, documented in test
comments rather than fixed: .fsd_study_id() is not vectorised (errors on
length>1 input, unlike every sibling id-extractor), and .mendeley_info()
does not classify a well-formed-but-nonexistent dataset id as an error
(Mendeley's API returns HTTP 200 with the real 404 only inside the JSON
body).
